- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply downward correction proportional to sentiment drop (e.g., 0.5x sentiment change).
- Model underperforms in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33); use 14-day EWMA or sentiment-weighted average for smoother forecasts.
- When true outcome is below 70, model often overcorrects; apply floor correction at 68–70 unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive negative values, model tends to underestimate; add 2–4% bias upward for next 5 days.
